caption: The drawing features a central, detailed depiction of a wooden statue representing a standing male figure dressed in traditional attire, with a feathered headdress and a belted tunic that extends to mid-thigh. The statue has long hair, and one hand rests on its waist while the other grips a long staff or pole that stands upright beside it. The coloration of the statue is predominantly brown and gray, illustrating the wood texture and weathered appearance, with some greenish and bluish tints indicating aged wood or residual paint. The base of the statue is rough and uneven, indicating it is carved from a single block of wood. On either side of the central image, there are line drawings of the same statue in profile, enclosed in rectangles. The left line drawing shows the statue from the left side, and the right drawing shows the statue from the opposite profile and includes measurements marked as “30” for height and “23” for width at the base. The entire composition is framed within a large rectangular border. The background is plain, light beige, allowing the statue and sketches to stand out prominently. At the bottom right, the text "INDIAN STATUARY IN U.S.A. XXXI" is inscribed.
title: Wooden Indian Chief
